intro: In Aydın province lie the remains of an Ionian city whose great temple became a landmark of ancient architectural design. This is the Ancient City of Magnesia ad Maeandrum, whose story begins in the 5th century BC, and which is famed for the Temple of Artemis Leukophryene.
history: The city was founded by Magnetes from Thessaly, and around 400 BC it was moved to a new site on the Lethaios river. Its golden age came under the Seleucids and the Kingdom of Pergamon, and in the Roman period it was an independent city. Carl Humann excavated here in 1891, and the work goes on: the site is still being excavated today.
structure-1: You are now before the Temple of Artemis Leukophryene, the masterpiece of the architect Hermogenes. It was dedicated to Magnesia's patron goddess, Artemis Leukophryene. Take a moment here: this is the building that made the city famous.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Theatre, the Agora, the Temple of Zeus and the Stadium.
facts: Did you know? Hermogenes' pseudodipteral Temple of Artemis established a plan type that the Roman architect Vitruvius cited as a model. The silt of the Maeander buried the city again and again; its stadium lay underground for centuries until excavation brought it back. And the temple's Amazonomachy frieze? Today it is split between museums in Paris and Berlin.
outro: This brings our journey through the Ancient City of Magnesia ad Maeandrum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
